title: Turkey fails in bid to recruit 11 athletes ahead of Los Angeles 2028 Olympics
content:
World Athletics has denied requests from 11 athletes to transfer allegiance to Turkey over what the sport’s governing body said “formed part of a coordinated recruitment strategy” by the Turkish government to attract athletes through lucrative contracts.

The athletes in question are mostly Jamaican field athletes and Kenyan distance runners, in addition to Nigerian sprinter Favour Ofili and Russian multi-eventer Sophia Yakushina.

Approving the switches would, World Athletics’ statement said, “impinge upon and compromise the imperatives underlying the World Athletics eligibility rules and transfer of allegiance regulations.”

The statement added that the “applications formed part of a coordinated recruitment strategy led by the Türkiye government acting through a wholly‑owned and financed government club, to attract overseas athletes through lucrative contracts, with the aim of facilitating transfers of allegiance and enabling those athletes to represent Türkiye at future international competitions, including the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.”

The Athletic has approached the Turkish Athletics Federation for comment. The decisions can be appealed and potentially taken to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Allegiance switching is commonplace in athletics — 32 athletes changed country in 2025, none to Turkey.

World Athletics president Sebastian Coe spoke out on the rules in 2020, when the process of allegiance switches for under-20s was made more complex out of safeguarding concerns.

Making the switch requires seeing out a three-year wait period before athletes can compete internationally. Word Athletics’ eligibility rules also state athletes must demonstrate they have a “genuine, close, credible and established link” to the country by the end of the waiting period, which starts from the date the application for approval is made to World Athletics.

Among the four Jamaicans in question are talented youngster Jaydon Hibbert, the world under-20 long jump champion in 2022, plus a trio of medallists from the 2024 Olympics in Paris. Wayne Pinnock, 25, won silver in the long jump, while Roje Stona earned a historic discus gold and Rajindra Campbell took bronze in the shot put.

The Athletic spoke to Stona and Campbell last summer about their decisions. “When this opportunity came up, I wouldn’t say it was a no-brainer, but it made a lot of sense professionally,” Stona, 27, said. “I had to look out for what is best for me, long term,” Campbell, then 29, said.

Most notable of the Kenyans is former women’s marathon world-record holder Brigid Kosgei. Aged 32, she is a six-time major marathon winner and 2020 Olympic silver medallist. Ronald Kwemoi, 30, who won 5,000m silver at the Paris Olympics, is another denied the switch.

Others include 23-year-old Relin Amanang’ole, who medalled at the World Road Running Championships in 2023, plus Brian Kibor, 25, Nelvin Jepkemboi, 24, Ofili, 23, and Yakushina, 20. The former is an alumni of Louisiana State University and the latter competes for Texas A&M.

Ofili finished sixth in the 200m Olympic final — and holds the national record with 21.96 secs — but was not able to compete over 100m in Paris because the Nigerian federation made administrative oversights and she had not been entered.

While these athletes cannot represent Turkey, there are no restrictions imposed on their involvement in one-day meetings or road races, and it is not under World Athletics’ jurisdiction to prevent them being based in the country or train there.

No Turkish athlete has won medals in track and field at the last two Olympics. At the 2024 European Championships, they took home two medals.
